sourceCopy.name: Statistical Power Calculator
sourceCopy.title: Statistical Power Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Estimate sample size or power for two balanced groups using Cohen’s d. Free, private, and calculated in your browser.
sourceCopy.intro: Plan a two-group comparison of means. Estimate power from a sample size, or estimate the participants needed for a target power.
sourceCopy.howAnswer: Power is the chance that a planned test detects the specified effect when that effect is real. It depends on the effect size, sample size and significance level.
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The calculation runs in this browser. Your assumptions are not uploaded or saved by this tool.
howTo: Choose whether to estimate power or sample size.
Enter Cohen’s d, the significance level and the target power or group size.
For sample size, optionally allow for expected participant loss, then review the estimate and its limits.

fields.sampleSizeMode: Estimate sample size for target power
fields.accuracyNote: Approximation for two independent, equally sized groups comparing means with a normal (z) model. It is not the exact small-sample t-test calculation.
fields.designNote: Cohen’s d is the expected difference between group means divided by the shared standard deviation. Use a defensible estimate from prior evidence or a meaningful minimum effect—not a result chosen after seeing the data.
fields.recruitedPerGroup: Recruit per group after expected loss
fields.formulaNote: The sample-size estimate rounds up to a whole participant. Recruitment allowance is calculated separately from the analyzed sample.

messages.checkInputs: Check the values and calculation mode.
messages.copyUnavailable: Copy is not available in this browser.
messages.sampleSizeTooLarge: The required sample is above this tool’s supported range.

additionalFaqs.question: What does 80% power mean?
additionalFaqs.answer: Under the assumptions entered, an 80% estimate means the planned test would detect the specified effect about 80% of the time if that effect were real. It is not an 80% chance that a result is true.

additionalFaqs.question: What is Cohen’s d?
additionalFaqs.answer: Cohen’s d is a standardized difference between two means: the expected gap divided by the common standard deviation. The result depends strongly on the effect you choose.

additionalFaqs.question: Does this replace a full power analysis?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. This browser estimate covers a balanced two-group means comparison with a normal approximation. It does not model unequal group sizes, paired data, proportions, ANOVA, clustered or repeated measures, covariates, exact t tests, multiple testing or study-specific design constraints.
